subject: Mathematics

definitions.definition: A number that can be expressed in the form p/q where p and q are integers and q is not equal to zero.
Rational numbers that represent the same value, e.g., 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent.
A rational number p/q is in standard form when q is positive and HCF of p and q is 1.

formulae.name: Addition of Rational Numbers
formulae.used_for: Adding two rational numbers with different denominators

formulae.name: Division of Rational Numbers
formulae.used_for: Dividing one rational number by another

important_concepts: Every integer is a rational number
Rational numbers are closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication
Rational numbers are NOT closed under division (dividing by zero is undefined)
Between any two rational numbers, there exist infinite rational numbers
Multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of p/q is q/p
common_mistakes: Forgetting to find LCM before adding rational numbers with different denominators
Not converting to standard form after operations
Confusing additive inverse with multiplicative inverse
Dividing numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator instead of multiplying by reciprocal
